chunks: Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Sufyan ibn Ya'qub ibn al-Harith ibn Ibrahim al-Hamdani, in a house in Kufa, narrated to us, saying: Abu Abdillah Ja'far ibn Ahmad ibn Yusuf al-Azdi narrated to us, saying: Ali ibn Yazid al-Hannat narrated to us, saying: Amr ibn al-Yasa' narrated to us, from Shu'ayb al-Haddad, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) say:

Indeed, our narration is difficult and hard to bear; it is not endured except by an Angel brought near, or a Prophet sent, or a servant whose heart Allah has tested with faith, or a fortified city. Amr said: Then I said to Shu'ayb: O Abu al-Hasan, and what is the fortified city? He said: Then he said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about it, and he said to me: The united heart.

key_terms.حَدِيثُنَا: Our narration (referring to the teachings of the Imams)
key_terms.عَبْدٌ امْتَحَنَ اللَّهُ قَلْبَهُ: A servant whose heart God has tested
key_terms.مَدِينَةٌ حَصِينَةٌ: A fortified city (metaphor for a strong mind/heart)
key_terms.نَبِيٌّ مُرْسَلٌ: A Prophet sent with a message

ai.seo_question: What does the 'fortified city' metaphor mean in Shia hadith regarding the depth of religious knowledge?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Ma'ani al-Akhbar* highlights the epistemological hierarchy of Shia gnosis, distinguishing between the external burden of complex traditions and the internal spiritual capacity required to bear them. The metaphor of the 'fortified city' as the 'united heart' underscores the Shia emphasis on *tawhid* (divine unity) as the structural integrity that protects the believer from the distortions of deep theological knowledge, a concept resonating with the Ismaili and Akhbari debates on the limits of human comprehension.

en.basel-kadem: 1.	We were told by Abu’l-Hasan, Ali bin Hussain bin Sufyan bin Ya’qoub bin Harith bin Ibrahim al-Hamdani in his house in Kufa, that he said: We were told by Abu Abdillah, Ja’far bin Ahmad bin Yusuf al-Azdi, that he said: We were told by Ali bin Yazid al-Hannat, that he said: We were told by Amru bin Yasa’, from Shu’aib al-Haddad, that he said: I heard Abu Abdillah, peace be upon him, say:

Indeed, our narration is difficult and complicated; it is not endured except by an Angel who is brought near (to Allah), or a Prophet that is sent (with a Divine Message), or a believer whom Allah has tested his heart with faith or a fortified city. Amru said: Then I said to Shu’aib: O Abu’l-Hasan, and what thing is a fortified city? He said: Then he said: I asked Abu Abdillah, peace be upon him, about it, and so he said to me: A united heart.
